case.paper_title: Human Capital and Development Accounting: New Evidence from Wage Gains at Migration
case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Immigrants with fewer than 9 years of schooling have larger log wage gains from the last home-country job to the last U.S. job than immigrants with at least 16 years of schooling.

tasks_info.task_instruction: In Task 1, the analyst was asked to conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: You should use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS (New Immigrant Survey) and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. You should not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e. whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.source_type: Survey-derived immigrant wage gain table from the New Immigrant Survey and Migration Projects
datasets.wave_or_subset: Authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx; treated as the pooled poor-country immigrant sample including Mexico because no separate source-file or wave indicator is available in the authorized data directory.
datasets.sample_size: 2854 rows in authorized file before analytic exclusions
datasets.notes: The authorized data directory contains one dataset file. The file has adjusted home and U.S. wages, education years, job years, sex, birth year, occupation groups, and country. It has no rural/urban upbringing column and no explicit NIS versus Migration Projects source indicator. Adjusted home wages contain a very large maximum, but the planned code does not choose outlier exclusions during planning.

files.name: wage_gain_table

summary_statistics.info: 2854 rows, 12 columns. Non-null count is 2854 for all columns. Numeric columns: edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, lastHomeWage, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWage, lastUsWageAdjusted. String columns: occGroupLastHomeJob, occGroupLastUsJob, country.
summary_statistics.describe: edyrs min 0, median 7, max 20. lastHomeWageAdjusted min 0.0183, median 4.2599, max 9504020.7036. lastUsWageAdjusted min 0.0010, median 12.0263, max 1247.8979. country has 10 categories: MEX 2376, PRI 228, DOM 76, NIC 42, SLV 40, GTM 28, COL 25, HTI 25, PER 9, ECU 5. occGroupLastHomeJob categories include Ag, Manufacturing, Services, Adminstrators, Education/arts, Professional/technical.

files.notes: The dataset contains occupation group variables that could proxy agriculture/nonagriculture sector, but Task2 prohibits controlling for sector. No region/rural variable exists.

estimand.outcome_scale: log units; exponentiated coefficient can be interpreted as an approximate percentage difference in wage gains
estimand.contrast: education group never_high_school, defined as edyrs < 9, versus college_degree, defined as edyrs >= 16
estimand.target_population: Immigrants represented in the authorized wage gain table, interpreted as the poor-country NIS and Migration Projects pooled sample including Mexico
estimand.time_scope: Wage at last home-country job versus wage at last U.S. job

inclusion_rules: Use observations with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages so that log wage gains are defined.
Use observations with non-missing education years and country.
exclusion_rules: Exclude observations with non-finite or non-positive adjusted wages.
Exclude observations with missing constructed education group, log wage gain, or country.

reference_specification.variable_construction: Use adjusted wages to form a log wage gain. Categorize edyrs into never_high_school (<9), some_high_school (9-11), high_school_some_college (12-15), and college_degree (>=16), with college_degree as the reference for the focal contrast.

conclusion_rule.expected_direction: The never_high_school minus college_degree contrast should be positive.
conclusion_rule.support_rule: The result maps to the focal claim by the sign and uncertainty of the never_high_school coefficient relative to college_degree; the planned candidate will report the coefficient, percent transformation, confidence interval, and p-value and will classify clear support only if the coefficient is positive with p < 0.05.

evidence.paper: The paper summary and focal claim state that wage gains on migration are compared by education and report that immigrants who have never been to high school gain more than immigrants with a college degree on p. 682. The paper data description states that pre- and post-migration wages are adjusted to comparable U.S. dollar values and wage gains at migration are central outcomes.
evidence.dataset_mapping: lastHomeWageAdjusted and lastUsWageAdjusted implement adjusted home and U.S. wages; edyrs implements schooling; country implements country categories for country fixed effects. Positive adjusted wages are required for logarithms.

uncertainties: The PDF tool provided a summary rather than exact table text, so the exact original standard-error method for the p. 682 education contrast is not stated.
The authorized file does not include an explicit data-source indicator or poor-country flag; the file is treated as the authorized pooled sample.

plan.path_summary: Estimate the education-gradient claim using log wage gains from adjusted wages and an education-group predictor that retains all schooling categories, extracting the never-high-school versus college-degree contrast. Task1 includes country fixed effects; Task2 uses the pooled sample with no sector or region controls.

path_signature.main_predictor: edu_group with college_degree reference and focal contrast never_high_school versus college_degree
path_signature.sample_restriction: Authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx; positive adjusted home and U.S. wages; non-missing constructed education group; Task1 also requires non-missing country.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for variables used in each task after reporting attrition.
path_signature.variable_construction: log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted); edu_group = never_high_school if edyrs < 9, some_high_school if 9 <= edyrs < 12, high_school_some_college if 12 <= edyrs < 16, college_degree if edyrs >= 16.
path_signature.inference_rule: Report focal coefficient, HC3 robust standard error, 95% confidence interval, p-value, and 100*(exp(coef)-1). Clear support if the focal coefficient is positive with p < 0.05; inconclusive if positive but p >= 0.05; opposite if negative with p < 0.05.

analysis_path.path_description: Use all education groups in the authorized data and estimate log wage gain on education category with country fixed effects, extracting the never-high-school versus college-degree coefficient.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Verify required columns edyrs, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, and country exist.
Report starting row count.
Keep rows with finite adjusted home and U.S. wages and report attrition.
Keep rows with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages so logarithms are defined and report attrition.
Construct log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Construct edu_group from edyrs: edyrs < 9 as never_high_school, 9-11 as some_high_school, 12-15 as high_school_some_college, and edyrs >= 16 as college_degree.
Drop rows missing log_wage_gain, edu_group, or country and report attrition.
Set college_degree as the reference category.
Estimate OLS log_wage_gain on edu_group and country fixed effects with HC3 robust standard errors.

Extract and report the coefficient for never_high_school relative to college_degree, its HC3 standard error, p-value, 95% confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, sample flow, and group counts.

key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Four-category education group based on edyrs, with focal contrast never_high_school (<9 years) versus college_degree (>=16 years).
key_choices.sample_restriction: Rows in authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx with positive adjusted home and U.S. wages, non-missing education group, and non-missing country.
key_choices.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion for non-finite/non-positive wages and missing model variables, with sample flow reported.
key_choices.data_processing: Log-transform adjusted wages; difference logs; categorize education; convert country to categorical fixed effects.
key_choices.model_choice: OLS with categorical education predictor and country fixed effects; HC3 robust covariance.
key_choices.inference_rule: Clear support if focal coefficient is positive and two-sided p < 0.05; inconclusive if same direction but p >= 0.05; opposite if negative with p < 0.05.

models.planned_estimation: Coefficient for never_high_school relative to college_degree in log wage gains, plus 100*(exp(coef)-1).
models.inference_criteria: Positive focal coefficient with p < 0.05 is classified as clear support; otherwise report direction and uncertainty.
models.qualification: The model directly estimates the education-group contrast in wage gains stated by the focal claim while adjusting for source-country differences available in the authorized data.

outcome.name: log_wage_gain
outcome.definition: Difference between log adjusted U.S. wage and log adjusted home-country wage for the same immigrant.
outcome.variable_construction: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), requiring both adjusted wages to be finite and positive.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Exclude rows with missing, non-finite, or non-positive adjusted wages.
outcome.qualification: The paper studies wage gains at migration using pre- and post-migration wages; log differences map naturally to percentage gains.

main_predictor.name: edu_group
main_predictor.definition: Categorical education attainment group derived from years of schooling.
main_predictor.variable_construction: edyrs < 9 = never_high_school; 9 <= edyrs < 12 = some_high_school; 12 <= edyrs < 16 = high_school_some_college; edyrs >= 16 = college_degree; college_degree is reference.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Exclude rows with missing edyrs or unclassifiable education group.
main_predictor.qualification: The focal claim explicitly compares never-high-school immigrants with college-degree immigrants; retaining intermediate categories avoids discarding the rest of the education distribution.

controls.name: country
controls.variable_construction: Included as categorical fixed effects C(country).
controls.qualification: Country fixed effects adjust for origin-country differences in wage levels and migration context while estimating education-group differences within the available country composition.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks estimate the wage-gain contrast directly named in the focal claim: no high school experience versus college degree. The log wage gain scale maps to percentage gains at migration.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both tasks use only the authorized original data file data/wage_gain_table.xlsx and verify all referenced columns before analysis.
method_justification.method_reason: OLS on log wage gains with categorical education groups provides a direct mean-difference estimate for the focal education contrast. HC3 robust standard errors are a defensible default for heteroskedasticity in observational wage data. Task1 uses country fixed effects to account for origin-country composition; Task2 omits sector and region controls as instructed.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Shared-memory paths restricted the analytic sample to only the two focal education endpoints and varied demographic, sector, country, or cohort controls. This path retains all education categories in the model and extracts the focal endpoint contrast; Task1 uses all education groups with country fixed effects, and Task2 uses all education groups in a no-control pooled model, so neither repeats prior candidates.

self_check.self_check_note: The focal claim and authorized dataset are unchanged. The generated scripts were read back. Referenced columns exist in the inspected dataset. The planned all-education-group approach is distinct from shared-memory paths that restricted to the two focal categories.

debugging_rule.repair_scope: Fix dependency installation, file path, or output extraction issues only; do not redesign the analysis, change variables, add or remove controls, alter sample restrictions, or change the focal claim.

execution_directives.comparison_metrics: Focal OLS coefficient for never_high_school versus college_degree on log_wage_gain, HC3 standard error, p-value, 95% confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, sample size, and conclusion classification.
